quick_skim.title: FELT: Generating Tactile Signals from Vision for Visuo-Tactile Manipulation
quick_skim.abstract: The sense of touch is central to manipulation, especially when vision is occluded or ambiguous. Although combining vision and touch improves manipulation, learning robust visuo-tactile policies requires substantial tactile data. Such data remains scarcer than visual data, because tactile sensors are fragile, specialized, and hard to standardize. To address this, we present Feature-Extracted Latent Tactile (FELT), a learning-based framework that synthesizes per-finger pressure tactile images from RGB observations, reducing the need for tactile-equipped data collection. FELT uses a large frozen visual encoder and a lightweight query decoder to predict tactile signals in a single feed-forward pass. To respect the physical topology of dual-finger tactile sensors, FELT decodes the left and right tactile sensor panels through separate branches, capturing the asymmetric contact patterns during interactions such as wiping, insertion, and in-hand rotation. At inference time, FELT only requires RGB data, allowing us to augment existing vision-only data with tactile observations, either as generated tactile images or as latent tactile features. Experiments on four contact-rich manipulation tasks demonstrate that both generated tactile images and latent tactile features improve policy success over vision-only baselines, with latent feature requiring no real tactile sensor during policy training or deployment. Supplementary material is available on our anonymous website: https://felt-tactile.github.io/.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: FELT generates per-finger pressure tactile images from RGB using a large frozen visual encoder and lightweight query decoder, reducing need for tactile data collection.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 触觉数据稀缺且难以获取，FELT框架通过冻结的视觉编码器和轻量查询解码器，从RGB图像预测每根手指的压力触觉图像，以单次前馈方式生成触觉信号，减少了对触觉传感器数据采集的依赖。实验表明该方法能有效合成逼真的触觉信号并提升视觉-触觉操纵性能，为多模态触觉感知提供了一种数据高效的解决方案。
